column3: Be just about to go out; attempt to go out
column5: ある朝、小狐が外へ出ようとして、「お母さん、目に何かが入った！痛い痛い！」と大きな声を出しました。
column6: One morning, just as the little fox was about to go outside, he cried out loudly, "Mom, something got in my eye! It hurts, it hurts!"
column7:
〜ようとする expresses being about to do something or making an attempt to do it.
Here it means the little fox was just about to go outside when the next event happened.

column3: Decide to do something for the child as a kindness
column5: 「かわいそうに...。町へ出て、この子に手袋を買ってあげよう」と思いました。
column6: \"Oh, you poor thing... I'll go into town and buy this child some gloves,\" she thought.
column7:
〜てあげる means to do something for someone else as a favor or kind action.
Here it appears in the volitional form 〜てあげよう, expressing the mother fox's decision or intention to do that kind act.

column3: Explanatory tone - it is the town's lights, not a star
column4: Plain form + んだ / Noun・な-adjective + なんだ
column5: 「あれは星じゃなくて、街の明かりなんだよ」と母狐は教えてあげました。
column6: \"That isn't a star, it's the lights of the town,\" the mother fox explained to him.
column7:
〜んだ adds an explanatory or clarifying tone.
Because 明かり is a noun, the form is なんだ.
The sentence-final よ adds emphasis, so なんだよ sounds like a clear, reassuring explanation.

column3: If the little fox goes, it might be okay
column4: Verb conditional (u-row -> e-row + ば / ichidan る -> れば / する -> すれば / 来る -> 来れば)
column5: 小さい小狐が行けば、大丈夫かもしれない。。
column6: If the little fox goes, it might be okay.
column7:
〜ば expresses a conditional meaning like "if" or "when that condition is met."
Here, 行けば presents going as the condition for the possibility that things will be okay.
This is the conditional form of 行く: 行く → 行けば.

Formation rules:
- Godan verbs: change the final u-row sound to the corresponding e-row sound, then add ば.
Example: 行く → 行けば, 読む → 読めば, 話す → 話せば.
- Ichidan verbs: replace る with れば.
Example: 食べる → 食べれば, 見る → 見れば.
- Irregular verbs: する → すれば, 来る → 来れば.

column3: Colloquial topic marking - as for humans, they are very scary
column5: 人間ってとても怖いものなんだよ。
column6: Humans are really scary creatures, you know.
column7:
〜って is a casual spoken topic marker.
Here, 人間って is similar to 人間は or 人間というのは, meaning "as for humans" or "humans, you know..."
It often introduces the speaker's view, explanation, or characterization in a conversational tone.

column3: Do exactly as the mother fox taught him
column4: Verb (dictionary/past) + とおり / Noun + のとおり
column5: 小狐は母狐に教えてもらったとおり、戸を手でトントン叩きました。
column6: The little fox knocked on the door with his hand, ton-ton, just as his mother had taught him.
column7:
〜とおり means "just as," "in the same way as," or "according to."
Here it shows that the little fox acted exactly in the way he had been taught.
In this sentence it follows the past form 教えてもらった, but it can also follow dictionary form verbs and nouns with の.

column3: Accidentally ended up putting out the fox hand instead
column5: 狐の手の方を出してしまいました。
column6: He accidentally ended up sticking out the fox hand instead.
column7:
〜てしまう can express either completion or an unintended / regrettable result.
Here it has the unintended-result nuance: the little fox made a mistake and ended up doing the wrong thing.
In this sentence it appears in the polite past form 〜てしまいました.

column3: So happy that it was almost enough to make her cry
column4: Noun / Verb plain form + ぐらい
column5: 小狐が帰って来ると、泣きたいぐらい喜びました。
column6: When the little fox came back, she was so happy she felt like crying.
column7:
〜ぐらい indicates degree or extent, similar to "so... that..." or "to the extent that...."
Here, 泣きたいぐらい means "to the extent that she felt like crying."
In casual usage, ぐらい and くらい are often interchangeable.

column3: Softly giving the reason - because he gave such warm, nice gloves
column5: こんなに暖かい、いい手袋をくれたもの。
column6: Because he gave me such nice, warm gloves.
column7:
Sentence-final もの can be used to give a reason or justification in a soft, emotional way.
It often sounds childlike, feminine, or intimate in tone.
Here it means something like "because, you see..." or "after all...."
A more neutral way to say this would be こんなに暖かい、いい手袋をくれたから or こんなに暖かい、いい手袋をくれたので.

column3: Wondering softly whether humans are really good after all
column5: 本当に人間はいいものかしら。。
column6: I wonder if humans really are good after all.
column7:
Sentence-final かしら expresses wondering or asking oneself something softly.
It often has a thoughtful, gentle, and traditionally somewhat feminine tone.
Here it shows the speaker quietly reconsidering whether humans might truly be good.
A more neutral equivalent would be 本当に人間はいいものだろうか or 本当に人間はいいのかな.
